title: House and Portrait
premise: Wendell Marchetti, a meticulous pest controller, is called to the Holloway farmhouse where something leaves fingerprints in flour dust and ash. His documentation habit becomes a lifeline as he discovers a sealed door beneath the property and a family that has been counting generations of things kept fed below. When an excavation crew breaches the door—sealed from the inside—the entity begins refilling the old well with bodies to replace what escaped. Wendell must smuggle the surviving Holloways out ahead of the count's completion, sacrificing his records, his reputation, and nearly himself; he burns the house and its ledger, choosing love for the last Holloway daughter over duty to the truth, though the final page of his journal suggests the count was never finished.
about_author: Lena Coldharbour is the pen name of a former rural insurance adjuster who spent a decade documenting claims in farm country, where she learned that paperwork can be a form of witness—or denial. She writes horror about ordinary people whose careful habits fail them beautifully.

chapters.title: Fingerprints in the Flour
chapters.summary: Wendell Marchetti arrives at the Holloway farmhouse on a routine rodent call and finds handprints pressed into flour dust—too large, too many joints. POV: Wendell. He photographs everything, cataloging with ritual precision. Emotional beat: unease masked by professional calm; documentation as prayer established.

chapters.title: The Client Who Won't Look at Him
chapters.summary: Maren Holloway hires Wendell but refuses to meet his eyes, insisting the problem is 'under the floor, not in it.' Her brother Elias watches from the stairs, counting under his breath. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the sense that the family knows more than they'll say, and pity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Bait That Comes Back Eaten
chapters.summary: Wendell sets traps; by morning every one has been emptied neatly, bait consumed, mechanisms untouched, arranged in a row facing the cellar door. POV: Wendell. He logs times, weights, patterns. Emotional beat: fascination overtaking fear—he realizes whatever this is, it is intelligent and courteous.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: The Holloways' neighbor sold the back field; surveyors arrive with ground-penetrating radar and find a void shaped like a room. Maren begs them to stop. POV: alternating Wendell and crew foreman Dale Pruitt. Emotional beat: dread of exposure—the family's secret is no longer containable.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Elias shows Wendell a family ledger: dates, tallies, offerings, going back to 1849. Every generation a keeper, every tally a life given so the rest could live. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: shame and resignation; duty inherited like a disease.

chapters.title: The Door, Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: The crew unearths a stone door bricked shut from within, its mortar finger-smeared. That night the fingerprints appear on Wendell's own truck windows, pressed from outside while he slept inside. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: violation—the watcher has become the watched.

chapters.title: Maren's Version
chapters.summary: Maren tells Wendell her childhood: the well, the monthly count, her mother teaching her which sounds meant hunger and which meant patience. She was supposed to be the next keeper. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: tenderness between her and Wendell kindles against shared terror.

chapters.title: Dale Breaks the Seal
chapters.summary: Against warnings, Pruitt's crew cracks the door with an excavator. The chamber beyond is empty except for scratch marks on the inner face—and a stairwell descending toward the old well. POV: Dale. Emotional beat: triumph flipping instantly to wrongness; silence where breathing should be.

chapters.title: The First Refill
chapters.summary: A crew member vanishes; his hard hat surfaces in the well, floating. The tally in the ledger updates itself in wet ink. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into arithmetic—the count has resumed, and it intends to balance.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Wendell compiles everything—photos, timestamps, the ledger—into a case file he plans to give police. But the sheriff who arrives reads the file, goes pale, and burns it in the sink. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: betrayal; justice outside the law revealed as the only justice available.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Grandfather's Debt
chapters.summary: The sheriff confesses his family were keepers before the Holloways; the county has always known. Evacuation would spread it. Containment is policy. POV: Sheriff Ansel Boone. Emotional beat: institutional cowardice; Wendell's faith in systems dies completely.

chapters.title: Counting Elias
chapters.summary: The entity takes Elias—not killed, but taken below, and the ledger marks him 'pending.' Maren shatters; Wendell holds her through the night while scratches rise up through the kitchen floorboards. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: grief fused with resolve; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Rain floods the region; the well rises, and with it the thing climbs closer to the house each night. Wendell maps its progress in his journal like tide tables. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grim competence as coping; the countdown structure becomes explicit.

chapters.title: Pruitt's Confession Tape
chapters.summary: A broken Pruitt records what he saw below—a room furnished for living, generations of habitation, then abandonment—and mails the tape to Wendell before walking into the well himself. POV: Dale (via tape). Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution; the enemy may be a forsaken resident, not a monster.

chapters.title: Two Keepers or None
chapters.summary: The ledger offers terms: the count completes at seven, or a new keeper binds it for another generation. Maren prepares to take the vow; Wendell refuses to let her. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the central choice sharpened—duty says sacrifice, love says run.

chapters.title: Getting the Family Out
chapters.summary: Wendell plans the extraction: Maren, her bedridden grandmother, and the ledger itself must cross the fields before dawn, before the seventh name. The grandmother refuses to leave, insisting the house needs a keeper. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: desperate logistics; tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: The grandmother writes her own name in the ledger to buy time, dying peacefully as the well exhales. The family flees across open ground while the thing stands at the tree line, patient, counting. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: sacrificial grace; fury at a system that eats its elders.

chapters.title: What Wendell Burned
chapters.summary: At the county archive, Wendell finds the original 1849 deed: the first Holloway didn't bind the thing—he freed it from a debt owed to the town, and the town made him its jailer forever. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: righteous anger; the crime was never the family's.

chapters.title: Before the Count Completes
chapters.summary: Wendell returns alone at night, ledger in hand, intending to write his own name and end the Holloway line's obligation. Maren follows him against every promise. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love arriving exactly where duty expected sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Well Room
chapters.summary: In the chamber, Wendell confronts the thing face to face—it wears the accumulated faces of every keeper who starved beside it. He offers the ledger closed: no more counts, no more keepers, just coexistence or nothing. It hesitates. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: climax; humanity offered to the inhuman.

chapters.title: Fire as the Final Entry
chapters.summary: Wendell burns the house, the ledger, and the door with Maren dragging him out as the well boils over and collapses into the aquifer. The count stops at six, incomplete, unsatisfied. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: catharsis through destruction; survival purchased with erasure.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wendell and Maren live quietly under new names. His recovered journal's final page bears fresh fingerprints in ash—one print, small, almost childlike, patient. Wendell does not document it. For the first time, he closes the book. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: ambiguous peace; some prayers go unanswered, and some should.
